logline: The staff of a Mumbai government hospital fight to save lives as the city is brought to its knees - first by the 2008 terrorist attacks, then by catastrophic urban flooding.

renewal.note: Two seasons completed as of October 2023. No formal greenlight for Season 3 announced as of mid-2026, though the series has maintained a returning schedule.

bollymeter.basis: 88% on Rotten Tomatoes from 8 critics; Film Companion called it one of the most compelling Indian shows of 2021. The hospital-during-26/11 frame turns a known catastrophe into an intimate ensemble study.

pull_quotes.text: Mumbai Diaries 26/11 is a riveting portrait of grace under pressure.
An urgent and swift series that feels authentic.
A gripping and poignant account of courage under fire.

seasons.review_body: Season 1, created by Nikkhil Advani, set the entire series at Bombay General Hospital during the night of November 26, 2008. The choice to contain the 26/11 attacks within a single institutional location proved formally smart: the show is not a reimagining of the attacks as spectacle, but a sustained portrait of the medical staff who received their casualties. Critics at 88 percent on Rotten Tomatoes converged on two strengths - Mohit Raina and Konkona Sen Sharma's lead performances, and the show's refusal to simplify its moral questions. Film Companion called it one of the most compelling Indian shows of 2021. The 79 percent audience score on Rotten Tomatoes indicated strong word-of-mouth.

episode_reviews.title: Nightmare Begins
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere drops the hospital into the attacks with minimum preamble. The show establishes its central cast and its central argument simultaneously: heroism at Bombay General is institutional, not individual. Critics noted the episode's controlled urgency as the series' strongest first impression.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The moment the first gunshot victims arrive and the hospital's inadequate capacity becomes the real emergency.

bollymeter.basis: 70% on Rotten Tomatoes from 10 critics; a strong audience score of 86% but critics found Season 2 less cohesive than the debut, with the flood-disaster premise producing more scattered storytelling.

pull_quotes.text: It isn't a flawless follow-up but it is one of those rare second seasons that boasts a distinctive identity.
As scattershot in execution and dreary to watch as the first season was gripping.

seasons.review_body: Season 2, released October 2023, shifted the crisis from the 26/11 attacks to the 2005 Mumbai floods, broadening the show's scope beyond the single-night containment that gave Season 1 its formal discipline. Critics at 70 percent were warmer in their audience response (86 percent Popcornmeter) but more divided in critical reception. The Times of India called it emotionally alive; Scroll.in found it scattershot. The consensus was that the flood premise, while compelling on paper, dispersed narrative energy that the hospital-siege structure had concentrated. Mohit Raina and Konkona Sen Sharma return with consistent authority; the show's faith in ensemble storytelling remains its core asset.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 2 trades the tightly concentrated single-night structure for a multi-day natural disaster, gaining scope but losing the formal focus that made Season 1 exceptional.
